clause_evidence.reasoning: Every sample asks students to determine something specific: a digit, a place, or a value. This central verb is instantiated across all 20 items through cloze completion, true/false evaluation, and multiple-choice selection. The verb drives the cognitive task.

Multiple-choice and cloze samples ask for the numerical value obtained by multiplying a digit by its position multiplier, or ask which place a digit occupies. Samples 4, 9, 11 explicitly compute values through multiplication shown in hints; samples 2, 5, 10, 12, 14, 19 ask for the place name. This requirement is robustly demonstrated across formats.

All 20 samples are constructed using 4-digit numbers (1695, 3250, 9105, 5210, 4725, 9501, 7639, 8735, 4120, 1305, 2360, 2410, 3165, 1845, 9034, 1524, 2406, 1630, 2415, 6015). No sample extends beyond four digits or contracts to fewer, ensuring consistent scope adherence.

Samples 3, 4, 6, 9, 11, 17, 18 explicitly address the value of a digit at its position through multiplication statements in stems and hints. For instance, sample 3 evaluates whether 5 in the ones place of 9105 has value 5; sample 4 asks for the place value (5 × 1000) of digit 5 in 5210. This decomposition is fully demonstrated.

Samples 1, 7, 8, 13, 15, 16, 20 ask students to identify which digit occupies a specified place position. Sample 1 asks what digit is in the ones place of 1695; sample 16 asks what digit is in the hundreds place of 1524. These samples directly address identifying a digit given its position in a number.

All 20 samples provide a place value context that anchors the mathematical task. Every item specifies a place (ones, tens, hundreds, or thousands) either explicitly or implicitly within the question structure. This context is essential to all tasks in the sample set.

cognitive_capacity.rationale: All 20 samples employ 4-digit numbers and foundational place value reasoning appropriate for Grade 3 Quarter 1 students. Computation demands are minimal, requiring only identification skills and basic multiplication at place value level, matching expected cognitive stage for early third grade mathematics instruction.

competency_alignment.rationale: Samples systematically address all three stated competency dimensions: identifying digits at specified places, identifying which place a digit occupies, and calculating digit values via place multiplication. The variety of question structures and numbers ensures alignment with the full competency scope without exceeding it.

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The six decomposed requirements map clearly across the sample set. Determine is central to every item; place value of digit is tested through both identification and calculation tasks; all items use proper 4-digit numbers; value of digit is explicitly demonstrated through multiplication scaffolding in hints; digit of number is directly assessed; place value context is provided throughout.

decomposition.reasoning: The six requirements capture the competency without loss. The column structure (determine the X, where X includes place value of digit, value of digit, digit of number, given place value context, working within 4-digit numbers) accounts for the full scope of the original competency statement. No significant competency clause exists that these six do not collectively address.

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: Coverage spans all place values (ones through thousands appear multiple times), both identification directions (digit-to-place and place-to-digit), and all three response formats (7 multiple choice items, 10 true/false items, 6 cloze items with fill-in-blank). Seeds range from 42 to 1002, indicating diverse generation pathways.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: All numbers stay within the 1000–9999 range appropriate for Grade 3 Quarter 1 place value instruction. No sample attempts to extend to five-digit numbers or introduce advanced operations beyond multiplication by standard place multipliers (1, 10, 100, 1000).

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The sample set demonstrates strong breadth: three distinct response formats are employed; true/false samples include both affirming and negating propositions; multiple choice options are constructed to include plausible distractors; theming is applied on 2 of 20 samples without interference; seed variation across 13 distinct values suggests robust generation diversity.
